source: Official complete-film uploads from REAL Skateboards, Santa Cruz Skateboards and Sci-Fi Fantasy, supplemented by independent filmographies, filmmaker portfolios and contemporary skate-media coverage

films.title: OVAL
films.description: REAL Skateboards' 35-minute first full-length in more than a decade brings the whole team into one film. Seven named full parts from Mason Silva through Zion Wright are linked by two team sections, expanding the documented roster to 18 skaters across a wide international filming itinerary.
creditNotes: REAL Skateboards' official upload labels OVAL a full-length, supplies the seven full-part names and chapter-level credits for two team sections.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies the 35-minute film, corroborates the complete 18-skater section structure and indexes the production credits.

Tim Fulton's Skatefolio credits Tim Fulton and Andres Garcia as filmmakers and identifies 24 additional filming contributors. Four further names indexed by SkateVideoSite are retained as additional production credits without invented roles.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite independently identifies San Francisco. The official rights-holder upload tags the remaining cities and regions; they are preserved as publisher-supplied filming geography rather than a claimed spot-by-spot itinerary.
films.historicalContext: OVAL was REAL Skateboards' first full-length in more than a decade and its first film in years to assemble the entire team, pairing seven complete parts with two cross-generational team sections.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It uses a dedicated REAL SKATEBOARDS PRESENTS OVAL title treatment beside a street-skating still and contains no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: REAL Skateboards' official channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and supplies the section structure and principal roster. YouTube reports channelId UCfAFEJj6edzegro3Tdn4B9A, a 2,089.561-second main-feature runtime and November 7, 2025 publication. The exact embed is allowed and advanced during controlled playback.
Independent filmography classifies OVAL as a 35-minute 2025 full-length, preserves the complete chapter structure, all 18 skaters, San Francisco context and the deep production-credit index.
Tim Fulton's filmmaker portfolio credits Fulton and Andres Garcia as filmmakers and distinguishes 24 additional filming contributors for OVAL.
Contemporary independent coverage identifies OVAL as REAL's first full-length in more than a decade.

films.title: TYPE
films.description: Santa Cruz Skateboards' 20-minute next-generation team film gives Devin Flynn, Taiga Nagai and Gabriel Ribeiro solo chapters, with Cole Gossett and Jan Hirt sharing a section. Two montages bring the complete official roster to 22 skaters.
creditNotes: Santa Cruz Skateboards' official upload identifies the project as its next-generation team film, supplies all 22 featured skaters and publishes the section timestamps.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies TYPE as a 20-minute full-length, corroborates all 22 skaters and credits Joe Perrin with the film.

Andrew Cannon's Skatefolio identifies Joe Perrin as director, Andrew Cannon as producer and nine named filmers. Four company production contributors indexed by SkateVideoSite are retained without unsupported role assignments.
films.locationNote: No reliable complete filming itinerary was located, so the record does not infer locations from the artwork or team affiliations.
films.historicalContext: TYPE introduced a 22-skater next generation of one of skateboarding's longest-running companies, combining emerging global riders in five named sections and two broad team montages.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It combines a dedicated graffiti-style TYPE wordmark with a street-skating still and contains no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

Independent filmography classifies TYPE as a 20-minute 2025 full-length, preserves the section structure, corroborates all 22 skaters and indexes five production contributors.
Andrew Cannon's filmmaker portfolio credits Joe Perrin as director, Cannon as producer and nine named filmers for TYPE.
Contemporary independent skate-media coverage identifies TYPE as Santa Cruz's new long-form video.

films.title: ENDLESS BEAUTY
films.description: Sci-Fi Fantasy's 37-minute debut full-length turns Jerry Hsu's art-driven company into a complete team film. Nine principal riders move through Los Angeles, New York and Chicago, with four additional documented appearances, while Matt King and Luke Murphy lead the edit and camera team.
creditNotes: Contemporary premiere and release coverage identifies the nine principal featured riders; Gabbe Eliassen is also billed as Gabriel Viking in contemporary shop coverage.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies the 37-minute film, expands the defensible appearance roster to 13 and indexes Los Angeles, New York and Chicago locations plus the production credits.

Bored of Southsea credits Matt King and Luke Murphy as editors and identifies the six principal camera contributors. Jerry Hsu's Skatefolio corroborates those roles and names 14 additional filming contributors. Remaining indexed names are retained as additional production credits without invented formal titles.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite identifies Los Angeles and New York City and maps Federal Plaza in Chicago; no broader city or spot itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: ENDLESS BEAUTY is the first full-length from Jerry Hsu's Sci-Fi Fantasy, translating the brand's photography, graphic design and surreal visual language into a 37-minute team film after a multi-city premiere tour.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is a film-specific candid of the crew embracing under a clear sky; the official upload title and independent full-length coverage establish the identity, and the image contains no trailer or episode labeling.
